analysis.title: Market Monitor, Week Ending November 13, 2026
key_insights: October US CPI rose 0.4% MoM (September: 0.6%), above the 0.3% consensus. Core CPI rose 0.3% MoM against a 0.2% consensus. No year-over-year CPI figures were published because no price data was collected during last year's government shutdown.

US PPI rose 0.3% MoM in October against a 0.4% consensus, but the year-over-year rate rose from 6.3% to 6.5%, the highest since 2022. Core PPI was 0.3% MoM (September: 0.8%) and unchanged at 5.0% YoY.

GSAM expects the Fed to hike 25 bp at the December meeting, and markets price an 88% chance of it. It sees consecutive hikes in December and January, then a prolonged pause, with more hikes possible if inflation proves sticky. Core CPI's 0.3% October gain is a 3.6% annualized pace and the third firm print in a row. GSAM reads the soft summer prints as transitory.

Price strength was broad across supercore (core services ex-housing), housing and core goods. GSAM argues this makes it less likely the Fed can look through the readings. It remains cautious on US rates given resilient growth and inflation momentum.

US Treasury yields rose on hot CPI, hawkish comments from Fed Governor Waller and weak demand at a 10-Year auction. The 2-Year ended at 4.84% and the 10-Year at 5.14%. The dollar index rose 1.09% to a 19-month high. EUR/USD ended at 1.1023 and USD/JPY at 159.71.

The S&P 500 rose 2.54% on the week on a tech recovery and lower oil, despite investor concern about developments at Nvidia. The STOXX 600 hit an all-time high (+2.49%) as some investors rotated to less AI-exposed European stocks. TOPIX gained 6.30% and KOSPI 4.56% after the prior week's tech rout.

S&P 500 EPS growth is tracking at 35% YoY with 80% of market cap reported, potentially the eighth straight quarter of double-digit growth. The median stock is growing 14%. GSAM says strong returns can continue if the absolute level of growth stays high.

GSAM calls the semiconductor sell-off a disconnect from fundamentals. Demand is running ahead of supply in memory, server CPUs and chip equipment. Memory makers are signing multi-year supply agreements and equipment makers are planning higher fab spending into 2027 and 2028. Demand is broadening from GPUs to CPUs, high-bandwidth memory, advanced packaging, networking and power.

GSAM sees Nvidia's leadership transition as more likely to shift share within semiconductors than to disrupt the broader AI investment cycle. It expects shifts to be gradual and to broaden the set of winners across GPUs, custom silicon and the supply chain.

Semiconductors trade at roughly 13x forward earnings, about 33% below their three-year average of 19x and near the 12.7x three-year trough, and below the S&P 500 multiple. GSAM says the market may already be discounting a meaningful earnings deterioration and that the correction is creating more attractive entry points, with a premium on selectivity.

Oil fell as President Trump said further strikes on Iran are quite unlikely and as signs of a global supply surplus and rising US crude inventories emerged. Attacks on tankers and Saudi oil infrastructure limited the losses. WTI ended at $88.56 and Brent at $95.84. Gold fell to $3,884.49 on the stronger dollar and higher yields.

Outside the US, China October CPI slowed to 0.7% YoY but PPI jumped to 5.7%, the highest since 2022. Euro Area Q3 GDP was confirmed at 0.4% QoQ, with France contracting and Italy flat. UK Q3 GDP grew 0.7% QoQ, the fastest since Q1 2024, driven by services and AI-related investment.
Bitcoin fell 9.19% on the week and is down 21.25% year to date. The VIX fell 24.73% on the week. Bloomberg US Aggregate lost 1.50% on the week as yields rose.

sector_views.rationale: Demand is outrunning supply and earnings expectations are holding up better than share prices imply. The group trades near 13x forward earnings, about 33% below its three-year average. GSAM calls the correction an attractive entry point but stresses selectivity.

earnings_insights: S&P 500 aggregate EPS growth is tracking at 35% YoY with 80% of index market cap having reported. This is a tracking figure and not final. Median stock EPS growth is 14%.
European companies are set to record their fastest profit growth in four years, per the report's description of earnings expectations. No figure is given.

Recent semiconductor earnings point to demand ahead of supply in memory, server CPUs and semiconductor manufacturing equipment, with management visibility extending beyond the next few quarters. No company-level EPS or revenue figures are given.

Weak demand at Treasury auctions, as seen at the 10-Year auction, adds to yield pressure.
Heightened scrutiny of the return on AI investment and developments at Nvidia.

vol_and_positioning: The VIX fell 24.73% on the week, is down 0.62% month to date, up 18.12% quarter to date and up 29.10% year to date.
US HY spreads tightened to 316 bps from 340 bps on October 31, and US IG to 86 bps from 90 bps. EUR HY tightened to 356 bps from 385 bps.
geopolitical: President Trump said further US strikes on Iran are quite unlikely, raising hopes of a resolution to the conflict and pushing oil lower.
Further attacks on tankers and on Saudi oil infrastructure limited oil's losses.
The report cites geopolitical and supply-chain considerations as added uncertainty for semiconductors.

tension_points.bull_case: Demand is running ahead of supply in memory, server CPUs and chip equipment. Memory makers are signing multi-year supply agreements and equipment makers plan higher fab spending into 2027 and 2028. The group trades near 13x forward earnings, 33% below its three-year average.
tension_points.bear_case: Competitive dynamics remain fluid and geopolitical and supply-chain considerations add uncertainty. The market may already be discounting a meaningful deterioration in future earnings.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Demand and earnings expectations falling to the weaker level the share prices imply, since GSAM says they are so far holding up better.
